title: Key Tips for Preventing Coolant-Related Tool Life Issues — MSC Industrial Supply Co.
summary: Understanding how coolant interacts with cutting tools can help reduce tool costs and improve surface finish. Proper coolant selection and maintenance plays a major role in any machining environment.
body_text: Coolant plays an essential role in the success of your operation, so following best practices is key to maximizing productivity and minimizing waste. Understanding how coolant interacts with cutting tools can help reduce tool costs and improve surface finish. Proper coolant selection and maintenance plays a major role in any machining environment. Before you panic about any potential loss of tool life, it’s important to consider coolant’s impact on your operation. By following coolant best practices, your team can easily improve the life of your cutting tools. Follow these steps to see how you can best utilize coolant to improve tool life: KEEP AN EYE OUT FOR EARLY WARNING SIGNS If your team notices an increase in coolant and tool expenses or poor surface finish, you may have coolant issues impacting tool life. Pro tip: Check if concentrations and pH are within the recommended range for your machine, material, and operation. MANAGE COOLANT CONCENTRATION AND CLEANLINESS Proper coolant maintenance is critical to maximize tool life. Keep concentrations in the recommended ranges, and ensure coolant is free of tramp oils, fines, and other contaminants. Clean and healthy coolant allows for the best possible tool life and surface finishes. IDENTIFY THE RIGHT COOLANT FOR YOUR NEEDS Have your operations, machines, or materials changed in the last few years? Work closely with your coolant supplier on your specific operation. Carefully selecting a high-performance coolant can optimize your tool life, improve productivity, and reduce potential downtime. Some metalworking fluids have a wide application and material range, such as TRIM® MicroSol® 692XT and TRIM MicroSol 685XT , while other coolants like TRIM C290 are used for more specific applications. LEARN WHAT COOLANT FACTORS IMPACT TOOL LIFE Metalworking fluids provide both lubricity and cooling to improve tool life and part quality. Slow speed, heavy duty operations may need a different coolant than high speed operations. Materials also play an important role and need to be considered. Understanding the effects of coolant selection, and its interaction with cutting tools will help maximize your tool life. STAY IN CONTACT WITH YOUR COOLANT SUPPLIER Keeping close contact with your coolant supplier will ensure you’re running the latest technology and best quality coolant for your machining. Pro tip: As your technology advances, your coolant should as well. Your coolant supplier will have the best insights on how to keep your tools running smoothly. PERFORM A COOLANT AUDIT Contacting your coolant supplier for an audit or consultation will help identify problem areas in your coolant use. By following their recommendations, you can prevent or even reverse many common tool life issues. This article was previously featured on Master Fluid Solutions' blog .

title: Custom Microgrids. Proprietary Intelligence. This Is NextNRG.
summary: Custom Microgrids. Proprietary Intelligence. This Is NextNRG.
body_text: A lot of companies will sell you solar panels and battery storage. Very few will design the entire system around your site's actual load profile, and fewer still have the proprietary technology to run that system intelligently once it's built. NextNRG does both. We design microgrids engineered to each site's specific infrastructure, energy demand, and resilience requirements, and we've built our own AI/ML technology to operate them. That combination, custom design plus proprietary control, is the core of what we do. Every Microgrid Is Designed Around the Site It Serves There is no one-size-fits-all microgrid. A cold storage facility runs a near-constant baseline load and can't tolerate even a short outage before product is at risk. A hospital has that same zero-tolerance for downtime, but its load spikes unpredictably with patient census and equipment use. A site with limited roof space or unfavorable solar orientation may lean almost entirely on storage and grid optimization instead of generation. None of these get the same system. NextNRG specifies the generation mix, storage capacity, and system architecture to the site: solar or alternative generation sized to the load, battery storage sized to peak demand and outage risk, EV charging infrastructure where relevant. Nothing is sold off a shelf, because no two sites carry the same risk profile or the same cost of getting it wrong. The Technology That Runs It: One Engine, Deployed at Every Scale Whatever the configuration, the microgrid components must be managed intelligently once installed. That's where the proprietary technology comes in. NextNRG's AI/ML technology is the same underlying system whether it's managing a single-site microgrid or optimizing infrastructure at the utility scale. At the site level, it's deployed as the Smart Microgrid Controller. At utility scale, the same technology is deployed as the Next Utility Operating System, or UOS. This technology continuously monitors system performance, forecasts power prices and load, and optimizes battery dispatch in real time, determining when to charge, when to discharge, and when to draw from the grid based on current conditions and what's forecast to come. RenCast, NextNRG's proprietary forecasting engine, feeds predictive weather intelligence directly into those dispatch decisions. What makes this hard to replicate isn't just that it forecasts and dispatches, it's what it's built to handle and how it decides. The controller is energy agnostic, supporting solar, battery storage, natural gas, diesel, microturbines, and other alternative fuel-based generation on a single platform. A site's generation mix doesn't dictate a different control system, which matters because most real-world sites end up with some combination of asset types, not a single clean technology. Dispatch decisions aren't governed by fixed rules or a static schedule either. The controller ingests real-time telemetry alongside predictive data, electricity market prices, weather, solar and load forecasts, fuel availability and pricing, and asset constraints, and re-evaluates dispatch on a rolling basis, typically every 15 minutes, with immediate response to abnormal events. Every decision balances operating cost, resilience, battery health , and site-specific priorities at once, rather than optimizing for one at the expense of the others. That's also why the technology doesn't require a full microgrid buildout to deliver value. NextNRG deploys it as a complete, custom-engineered infrastructure solution, or as standalone technology, including cloud-based SaaS, for organizations that already operate generation and storage assets and need the intelligence layer on top. The Dashboard: Seeing and Directing What the System Is Doing All of this intelligence needs a way for the people running a facility to actually see it and act on it. That's what the NextNRG Dashboard is for. It's the interface that sits on top of the controller, giving operators real-time visibility into generation, storage, and grid interaction in a single view. It also extends beyond the microgrid itself. A logistics operation running a mixed fleet, part EV, part traditional combustion, can track fuel consumption and charging activity side by side instead of juggling two separate systems. Predictive maintenance flags anomalies and routes service alerts before small issues become downtime. Carbon tracking turns generation and storage data into a reportable record of environmental impact, useful for organizations that need to show that number to a board, a regulator, or a customer. The NextNRG Dashboard doesn't operate the microgrid. It's the visibility layer, showing what the microgrid, the controller behind it, and increasingly the rest of the operation, is doing in real time. What NextNRG Builds NextNRG designs custom microgrids for commercial and industrial facilities, healthcare campuses, municipal operators, tribal lands, and government sites, engineered to each site's infrastructure and operated on our own proprietary AI/ML technology from deployment. Contact the NextNRG team at nextnrg.com to discuss what a microgrid designed for your site would look like. title: Top AutoRFP Alternatives & Competitors For 2026
summary: The best AutoRFP alternatives and competitors for 2026, compared on automation depth, content reuse, pricing, and which teams each tool actually suits.
body_text: If you're comparing AutoRFP alternatives, you already know the trade-offs, the library upkeep, the generic drafts that need rewriting, the slowdowns as RFP volume grows. The real question is which tool fixes the problem your team keeps running into. This guide compares the top AutoRFP alternatives such as Inventive AI, Loopio, Qvidian, AutogenAI, Responsive, and Proposify, on features, strengths, limitations, and pricing, so you can match one to how your team actually works. Key Insights AutoRFP alternatives: The AI-native alternatives built for context-aware responses are Inventive AI and AutogenAI; the established platforms built around content libraries, workflows are Loopio, Responsive, Qvidian, and Proposify. Why teams switch: constant library upkeep, no CRM or call-data context, limited template flexibility, no win/loss analytics. When AutoRFP still fits: moderate volume, a dedicated content owner, a maintained library, it's rated 4.8/5 on G2 for exactly that. How to choose: match the tool to your main problem; response quality, governance, enterprise coordination, or ease of use. Why teams look for AutoRFP alternatives AutoRFP.ai is well-rated, 4.8/5 across G2 reviews , with users reporting around 60% time savings on responses. It works best for teams that respond to a moderate number of RFPs and have someone maintaining a well-organized answer library. Teams start looking for alternatives for a few specific reasons: The answer library needs constant upkeep. Auto-fill reaches roughly 60% when the library is well maintained, but accuracy drops as stored answers go out of date, so results depend on having someone responsible for keeping content current. No live deal context. AutoRFP.ai answers only from your stored answer library, not from your CRM or call recordings (such as Gong), so responses aren't tailored to a specific buyer, industry, or deal stage. Limited analytics. There's no win/loss tracking or outcome reporting, so teams can't easily measure which responses win deals or improve over time. Not the most intuitive to use. Reviewers say the platform takes time to get comfortable with, and teams often need formal training before they can use it efficiently day to day. Complex questionnaires are harder to handle. Large or non-standard formats like long security questionnaires or multi-tab spreadsheets strain the tool as they scale. Also Read: AutoRFP vs Inventive AI: Which Wins More Deals? Top AutoRFP Competitors and Alternatives We compare the eight strongest AutoRFP alternatives on strengths, limitations, pricing, and best-fit team, so you can find the right match fast. Tool Overview Key differentiator Pricing (2026) G2 rating Inventive AI Autonomous, agentic RFP, RFI, and DDQ automation with human approval for Mid-enterprise teams Connect existing systems → contextual responses → conflict and outdated content checks → better quality and cited responses Usage-based, unlimited users 4.9/5 Arphie AI-native RFP automation for lean teams Auto-fills RFPs and questionnaires from connected knowledge, no static library Custom quote (per-project) 5/5 1up Fast, self-serve setup for sales and IT teams Generates answers from existing docs; Q&A inside Slack and Teams Free; Starter $300/mo; Plus $900/mo; Enterprise custom 4.9/5 AutogenAI AI bid and proposal writing Fast first drafts with built-in bid project management Custom quote 4.3/5 Loopio Content library management + governance Structured Q&A library with tagging and approval workflows Median around $23,915/year, depending on tier 4.6/5 Responsive (formerly RFPIO) Enterprise, multi-team proposal operations Deep governance, granular permissions, and analytics at scale $5000/yr; quote-based 4.5/5 Qvidian (Upland) Template-driven, repeatable proposals Central content repository + structured templates ~$15,000–25,000/yr; quote-based 4.3/5 Proposify Proposal design + e-signatures Branded, interactive proposals with engagement tracking Basic $29/user/mo; Team $49/user/mo 4.6/5 1. Inventive AI Inventive AI is an autonomous, AI agentic software for RFPs, RFIs, DDQs , and security questionnaires. The agents work from the systems your team already uses, draft contextual responses, and keep humans in the loop for approvals, so teams stop maintaining a Q&A library and stop drafting from scratch. Best for: Mid-market and enterprise proposal, presales, and InfoSec teams that want to cut manual drafting and library upkeep while keeping approval control. What sets it apart AI-generated first drafts: Reads the RFP and drafts every answer from your connected knowledge, so teams start from a near-complete draft, not a blank page. Knowledge Hub: Connects SharePoint , Salesforce , Google Drive , Confluence , and more into one live source that updates automatically, so there's no Q&A library to maintain. Context Engine: Uses deal and customer context so each answer fits the specific opportunity, not generic library copy. Content Governance Agent: Flags outdated, conflicting, or duplicate content automatically, no content owner needed. Cited, confidence-scored answers: Every response shows sources and a confidence score, and flags "information unavailable" instead of guessing. Strategic agents: Go/No-Go checks deal fit early, the Competitive Intelligence Agent positions you against named competitors, and the Full Response Analyzer catches gaps and contradictions before submission. Format flexibility: Handles both Excel-based questionnaires and long-form narrative proposals in one workflow. Review and approval workflow: Assign sections, track progress, approve, with approved answers flowing back into the Knowledge Hub. Inventive product image Strengths Rated the #1 easiest-to-use RFP tool on G2 , with fast adoption and minimal onboarding. Quick to implement compared with traditional library-based tools. High-quality, contextually accurate first drafts that need little editing. Customer support is frequently praised as responsive. Limitations Mobile experience is thin, hard to review drafts from a phone between meetings. Analytics are limited for ROI tracking and QBR-style reporting. No native Gong integration yet for conversation-intelligence data. Focused on RFPs, RFIs, and DDQs, not battlecards, pre-call briefs, or broader sales collateral. Pricing Simple and transparent, usage-based with unlimited users. What customers say about Inventive AI A verified G2 review (Snehil S., 4.5/5) says it's the easiest RFP tool to teach, with users productive in 5–6 days vs 2–3 weeks on legacy tools; the one gripe is a weak mobile experience with no native app. Better answers win more RFPs. See how context-aware responses, tailored to each buyer, improve win rates, not just turnaround time. Book a demo → 2. Arphie Arphie is an AI-native platform for RFPs, RFIs, DDQs, and security questionnaires, built around human-in-the-loop workflows. It connects to your business information where it already lives, so there's no Q&A library to assemble or update. Best for: Lean sales, solutions, and security teams that want AI-native automation without maintaining a library. What sets it apart Connects to information where it lives : Draws answers from existing sources rather than a Q&A library, cutting setup and upkeep. Transparent AI drafts : Every first draft shows its source citations and confidence signals, so reviewers can trust and verify fast. Automatic freshness checks : Flags responses that may be outdated when the underlying documents change. Strengths Reviewers consistently report major time savings on responses. Intuitive interface and easy onboarding. Scores high on meeting requirements, usability, and ease of setup. Limitations No mobile support as reported by reviewers. Limited import/export formats, Excel is primary; Word and PDF are still developing. Less mature Salesforce integration than some alternatives. Does not have competitive intelligence ability to check competitors trends before responding Pricing Custom quote (per-project model). What customers say about Arphie According to G2, a verified customer (Ujjal M., 5/5) says its Dynamic Option feature delivers faster, higher-quality answers with less cleanup; the drawback is inconsistent reviewer auto-assignment when new questions are added. 3. AutogenAI AutogenAI is an AI-first platform for proposal and bid writing that helps teams draft compliant proposals and manage the full bid process in one place. Best for: Bid and proposal teams handling high volumes of tenders with strict response requirements. What sets it apart Bid-focused drafting: Generates first drafts tuned to bid and tender requirements, saving time upfront. Gamma Review: Automates requirement extraction and compliance checking so drafts meet response criteria. Citation-backed RAG: Forces the AI to cite corporate history and brand-approved language, keeping outputs on-message. Strengths Reviewers consistently cite faster first drafts. Feels built for bid writing rather than a generic AI tool. Useful with large volumes of tender information and technical input. Limitations No built-in graphics or charts, so teams rely on other tools for visuals. Version control and real-time editing feel basic for multi-user work. High-risk responses still need manual accuracy and compliance checks. Minimum seat commitments and onboarding fees make it hard for smaller teams. Pricing Custom quote (enterprise). What customers say about Autogen AI A verified G2 review (Tobias O., 4.5/5) praises its agentic AI capabilities and responsive trainer, but flags performance lags and difficulty assigning specific templates to an analysis. 4. 1up 1up helps sales and IT teams answer RFPs, security questionnaires, and everyday sales questions fast. It connects to existing content sources and delivers respnses inside the tools reps already use, without a separate Q&A library to maintain. Best for: Sales and pre-sales teams that need instant, trusted answers inside Slack, Salesforce, or a browser. What sets it apart Answers in your workflow: Works inside Slack, Teams , and Salesforce, so reps get answers without switching tools. Conversational Q&A: Reps ask questions in natural language and get instant, sourced answers for live deals. Broad use cases: Handles RFPs, security questionnaires, and everyday sales questions, not just formal RFPs. Strengths Setup is fast, often live within a couple of days. Reviewers praise its speed and ease of use. Support is responsive and quick to act on feedback. Limitations It struggles with complex, multi-part questions and can return inaccurate answers. It is not a full RFP project tool, with no approval workflows, multi-gate review, or document assembly. Analytics are lighter than some teams expect. Answer quality depends on how well content is kept current. Pricing Free plan; Starter $300/mo; Plus $900/mo; Enterprise custom. What customers say about 1up According to G2, a verified customer (Tristan B., 5/5) says it centralized scattered info with strong Slack Q&A and setup in days; the only dislike is adjusting to the web editor after Excel. Also Read: 1Up vs AutoRFP: Best RFP Tools for 2026 5. Loopio Loopio is a response management platform built around a centralized content library and structured team workflows, used for RFPs, security questionnaires, and DDQs. Best for: Teams formalizing their RFP process for the first time who want fast onboarding. What sets it apart Centralized library: Stores approved answers with tags and categories, so content is easy to find and reuse. Magic AI suggestions: Surfaces responses from approved content to speed up drafting. SME workflows: Assigns questions and tracks progress, keeping multi-contributor projects organized. Strengths Fast and intuitive, so teams onboard quickly. Reliable for repetitive, well-covered questions. Support and implementation help are frequently praised. Limitations The library needs ongoing upkeep or answer accuracy drops. The AI respond from a static library rather than drafting context-aware answers, so responses often need rewriting. There is no conflict detection, so contradictory or outdated answers go unnoticed unless caught manually. User-based pricing gets expensive when adding many occasional contributors. AI was added to an established Q&A platform rather than built in from the start, so drafts often need editing. Loopio product image Pricing Median around $23,915/year, typically $11,770 to $58,277 depending on tier ( Vendr data) What customers say about Loopio A verified G2 review (Vijay R., 4.5/5) calls the Library its best asset with context-aware suggestions, but notes heavy upfront library-building and search that returns too many loose matches. Also Read: Loopio vs Responsive: Which RFP Software Is Better in 2026? 6. Responsive (formerly RFPIO) Responsive is an enterprise response management platform for RFPs, security questionnaires, DDQs, and proposals at scale. Best for: Large, multi-department teams with complex, high-volume proposal operations . What sets it apart AI retrieval and drafting: Ask and LookUp generate source-cited drafts, with TRACE Score validating responses. Broad integrations: Close to 30 native integrations plus 75+ open APIs for custom workflows. Enterprise workflow: Handles multi-team routing, permissions, and large-scale project orchestration. Responsive product image Strengths Handles complex, high-volume questionnaires well. Offers deep CRM coverage, granular permissions, and strong analytics. Reviewers note frequent AI and feature updates. Limitations The feature-dense interface has a steeper learning curve. The AI can generate answers from outside approved content, per user reports. Costs are higher and harder to forecast with per-user licensing and add-ons. TRACE Score checks individual answers but does not catch contradictions across the library. Pricing From $5,000/year (Lite, 5 users); mid and enterprise tiers custom-quoted. What customers say about Responsive According to G2, a verified customer (Rui D., 4/5) likes its constant AI updates and powerful filtering, but cites trouble importing complex Excel files and occasional slowness that loses entered content. 7. Qvidian (Upland) Qvidian is a proposal and RFP response platform built around a central content repository and structured templates, best suited to standardized, repeatable proposals. Best for: Teams with highly standardized proposals and repeatable content needs. What sets it apart Central repository: Stores approved responses and corporate content for consistent reuse. Template-driven assembly: Builds proposals from structured templates for uniform formatting. Office integration: Microsoft Office plug-ins make it familiar for Office-based teams. Strengths Strong content storage and reuse that makes libraries more effective. Intuitive interface with robust search. Familiar for teams that already work in Microsoft Office. Limitations Uploading and updating content is manual and time-consuming. Search lacks a semantic approach, so the best answers are not always surfaced first. Reporting is rigid and often needs custom setup for routine data. AI was added to an older template-based platform and is still maturing, so it does limited context-aware drafting. Pricing Around $15,000 to $25,000/year, quote-based ( vendr data ). What customers say about Qvidian A verified G2 review (4/5) says proposal creation is efficient with easy search, but wants semantic search and finds uploading and updating data difficult and time-consuming. 8. Proposify Proposify is a proposal design and e-signature platform for creating branded, interactive sales proposals and tracking engagement. Best for: Sales teams that need polished, on-brand proposals and quotes, not large-scale RFP automation. What sets it apart Design-locked templates: Reps edit text but cannot break branding, so proposals stay on-brand. Interactive pricing and e-sign: Built-in quoting and signatures close deals in one document. Engagement tracking: Shows when prospects open and read proposals, guiding follow-up. Strengths Easy to create professional, visually appealing proposals. Templates keep every proposal on-brand. Engagement tracking helps teams time their follow-ups. Limitations Customization and layout flexibility frustrate some users. It cannot auto-answer large or complex RFPs. The Basic plan caps sends at 5 per month for up to 2 users, forcing upgrades. It covers proposals and quotes only, not contracts or broader document workflows. Pricing Basic $19/user/month; Team $49/user/month. What customers say about Proposify According to G2, a verified customer (Nick H., 2.5/5) values the HubSpot integration and template library, but finds the editor clunky, edits that don't save, and awkward pricing tables. How to choose the right AutoRFP alternative The best alternative is the one that fixes your specific bottleneck. Match your main challenge to the tool. If your main challenge is Consider Why Library upkeep is hurting answer accuracy Inventive AI, Arphie Both work from your existing systems- Notion, Slack, Confluence, Salesforce, Hubspot and more so there is no Q&A library to maintain Reps need fast answers inside Slack or Salesforce 1up Answers questionnaires and sales questions directly in the tools reps already use Deal-specific response quality and AI governance Inventive AI Context Engine tailors each answer per deal, with citations and automatic content checks High-volume bids and tenders with strict compliance AutogenAI, Inventive AI Built for bid writing, with requirement extraction and compliance checking Formalizing your RFP process for the first time Loopio Structured library and workflows with fast onboarding Enterprise, multi-team proposal operations Responsive Deep governance, permissions, integrations, and analytics at scale Standardized, repeatable proposals Qvidian Template-driven assembly from a central content repository Polished, on-brand proposals and e-signatures Proposify Design-locked templates, interactive pricing, and engagement tracking Make Your Next RFP Response Faster to Win The right alternative fixes your specific problem. For library upkeep and accuracy, look at AI-native tools like Inventive AI, Arphie, or 1up. For enterprise governance, Responsive or Loopio. For on-brand proposals, Proposify. If AutoRFP still handles your volume, you may not need to switch. Before committing, shortlist two tools and run a real RFP through each in the trial, using your own content and a few edge-case questions. Confirm pricing, data-security terms, and implementation time in writing. AI built for RFPs from the ground up. Inventive AI delivers 2x better response quality, as reported by RAD-AI. Book a demo → FAQs Do AutoRFP alternatives keep my data private, or train AI on it? Most keep it private. AutoRFP alternatives like Inventive AI and 1up state customer data is never used to train public models, and most are SOC 2 Type II compliant . Confirm data residency and training-data terms in the contract. Are AutoRFP alternatives more accurate than AutoRFP? AI-native alternatives ground answers in your approved content with source citations and confidence scores, and report accuracy around 95 percent. Like AutoRFP, they still need manual review on pricing, legal, and compliance answers. How long do AutoRFP alternatives take to implement? Library-based alternatives like Responsive and Qvidian take 4 to 8 weeks. AI-native alternatives like Inventive AI, Arphie, and 1up can be live in days, since there is no library to build first. Which AutoRFP alternatives handle security questionnaires and DDQs? Inventive AI, Arphie, Responsive, and 1up cover RFIs , DDQs , and security questionnaires . Proposify does not, since it focuses on proposal design. How hard is it to switch from AutoRFP to another tool? The main cost is migrating and re-tagging your content, heaviest for library-based tools. Alternatives that read from existing systems reduce it. Confirm data export terms before signing. Do AutoRFP alternatives still need a dedicated content manager? Library-based ones like Loopio, Responsive, and Qvidian do, or accuracy drops. Alternatives with automated governance, like Inventive AI, reduce that need by flagging outdated content automatically. ‍

title: How to Charge a Virtual Credit Card Without a POS Device

But what if you need to charge your virtual cards without a traditional point-of-sale (POS) device? We've got you covered with some quick payment solutions to tackle this challenge head-on.
body_text: With Tab, you can charge OTA virtual credit cards without a physical POS device. You use Tab’s web dashboard to enter the virtual card number, expiry date, CVV, exact booking amount, and card currency, then process the payment from your browser. Because Tab is built for tourism businesses, it’s a practical way to charge Booking.com, Expedia, Agoda, and other OTA virtual cards even if you don’t have a traditional card terminal. Leverage Online Payment Gateways Popular channel managers like Sirvoy may allow you to charge virtual cards, as long as you have an account with payment platform Stripe and the right merchant category code (MCC). But what if I can’t get a Stripe account in my country? Tab works in most countries and most currencies, with a bespoke payment feature built especially for charging virtual credit cards , all from your web browser. How to charge a virtual credit card without a POS device Some web-based payment platforms allow merchants to manually enter virtual card details and process secure transactions securely, without a physical POS device. Services such as Tab offer a desktop web app that’s user-friendly and can process your virtual card payments in a matter of seconds. After you apply for an account with Tab, and the account is approved, you can start taking payments. For virtual cards, you can input the details provided by the card provider in your Tab dashboard and immediately charge the card. However, virtual cards can be expensive to charge, so you may want to explore alternatives! Receive Your OTA Payments via Another Method While virtual cards streamline OTA transactions, they may pose challenges for tourism businesses that can’t charge them. They’re usually more convenient for the OTA provider than for the business! If you already receive virtual credit cards, you might want to explore the other ways that you can take payment from OTAs like Booking.com and Expedia. You could ask them to send your funds via bank transfer, or request to receive the secure customer card details when they book via the platform. You can then charge the details through your POS or another payment provider. This opens up more traditional (and cheaper!) payment options - for example, Tab can help you charge secure customer card details provided by Booking.com and Expedia. It’s a great way to secure your bookings in advance, and we can send your weekly payments (we call them payouts) to most bank accounts in most currencies around the world. Our Tips: Check if the virtual card provider can pay you via another method, such as bank transfer. Sign up for a free Tab account and charge virtual cards without the need for hardware! Conclusion: Receiving your money on virtual credit cards with no way to charge them may seem daunting, but with the right online payment tool, it’s easy. Ready to charge virtual cards without a POS device? Apply for a Tab Payments account today , and start charging OTA virtual cards from your browser. By Raghvi Arya. title: Redwire Announces Major Expansion in Huntsville, Scaling Production of Combat-Proven UAS and Mission-Critical Space Infrastructure
summary: Expanded campus will create new high-tech jobs and increase advanced manufacturing capacity FARNBOROUGH, England – (July 20, 2026) – Redwire Corporation (NYSE: RDW), together with the State of Alabama…
body_text: Expanded campus will create new high-tech jobs and increase advanced manufacturing capacity FARNBOROUGH, England – (July 20, 2026) – Redwire Corporation (NYSE: RDW), together with the State of Alabama and the City of Huntsville, today announced a major expansion of Redwire’s Huntsville campus, reinforcing Alabama’s position as a national leader in aerospace, defense, and advanced, U.S.-based manufacturing. Redwire is adding 164,000 square feet to its operational footprint in Huntsville, increasing the company’s manufacturing and engineering capacity to develop and produce mission-critical technologies that strengthen America’s leadership in space and provide advanced capabilities to the U.S. military and its allies. Supported by approximately $8.5 million in eligible state and local economic development incentives, Redwire is expected to create approximately 150 new high-skilled jobs spanning engineering, manufacturing, integration, and technical operations. Construction has already begun on the expanded campus, with building expected to be completed by Q4 2027. The expanded campus will accelerate Redwire’s production of combat proven Stalker UAS, Octopus gimbal payloads, advanced energy solutions, and space capabilities that support exploration, commerce, and national security. By expanding U.S.-based production of these essential capabilities, Redwire is strengthening critical domestic supply chains while helping to ensure America remains at the forefront of aerospace and defense innovation. Quote from Peter Cannito, Chairman & CEO, Redwire “Expanding the footprint Redwire has established in Huntsville reflects the momentum we’re seeing across both Redwire Space and Defense Tech,” said Peter Cannito, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Redwire. “Huntsville is one of the fastest growing technology hubs in the United States, uniquely positioned at the intersection of America’s space and defense industries, which makes it the ideal location to expand our capabilities and strengthen America’s industrial base. We’re grateful to Governor Ivey, Mayor Battle, and our state and local partners for helping make this strategic growth possible and for their continued commitment to developing Alabama’s high-tech economy.” Quote from Alabama Governor Kay Ivey “Alabama is proud to be at the forefront of innovation that strengthens our national security, advances space exploration and creates meaningful, high-paying careers for our people. Redwire’s expansion in Huntsville is a powerful endorsement of our state’s skilled workforce and collaborative business environment, and it further solidifies Alabama’s leadership in aerospace and defense.” Quote from Huntsville Mayor Tommy Battle “Redwire’s continued investment is another strong vote of confidence in Huntsville’s world-class aerospace and defense ecosystem, creating 150 new high-quality jobs while building on the talented team already here. We’re proud to welcome their expansion and look forward to supporting their continued success as they help shape the future of space and national security,” said Huntsville Mayor Tommy Battle. Quote from Alabama Secretary of Commerce Ellen McNair “Redwire’s buildout in Huntsville is a testament to the company, its product and its mission. title: CVE-2026-8933: Local Privilege Escalation in Set-Capabilities snap-confine
summary: Qualys TRU discovered CVE-2026-8933, a High-severity Local Privilege Escalation in snap-confine affecting Ubuntu Desktop 24.04, 25.10, and 26.04. Learn detection with Qualys QIDs and how to remediate.
body_text: Table of Contents What is the Attack Surface for CVE-2026-8933? Exploitation Mechanism Affected Versions & Remediation Technical Details of the CVE-2026-8933 Acknowledgments Qualys QID Coverage for Detecting CVE-2026-8933 Discover Vulnerable CVE-2026-8933 Assets with Qualys CyberSecurity Asset Management Automatically Patch CVE-2026-8933 with Qualys Patch Management The Qualys Threat Research Unit (TRU) has identified a Local Privilege Escalation (LPE) vulnerability in snap-confine (CVE-2026-8933). This flaw allows an unprivileged local user to gain full root access on default installations of Ubuntu Desktop 24.04, 25.10, and 26.04. The issue stems from a security hardening change that inadvertently introduced a race condition during sandbox initialization. What is the Attack Surface for CVE-2026-8933? snap-confine is the enforcement component that builds the execution environment for snap applications. In recent Ubuntu releases, Canonical shifted snap-confine from a set-uid-root binary to a set-capabilities model to enforce least privilege. While intended to reduce the attack surface, this change means snap-confine now executes with the effective UID of the calling user while retaining near-root capabilities. During sandbox setup, the binary creates temporary directories and files under /tmp that are initially owned by the unprivileged user. Ownership is transferred to the root shortly after, but a narrow window remains during which the caller retains full control. Exploitation Mechanism CVE-2026-8933 is rated High severity. The exploit leverages two concurrent race conditions. First, an attacker mounts a FUSE filesystem over the temporary scratch directory immediately after creation. This bypasses the mount namespace isolation snap-confine applies later, keeping the directory accessible outside the sandbox. Second, the attacker creates a symlink pointing to an arbitrary target file. When snap-confine attempts to create a sandbox file, the open() call follows the symlink and writes to the target. A second race condition allows the attacker to widen file permissions to 0666 before snap-confine calls fchown() to transfer ownership to root. To bypass AppArmor confinement, the exploit targets the /run/udev/** path, which permits read-write access. By dropping a malicious .rules file in /run/udev/rules.d/ and triggering a FUSE mount/unmount cycle, the attacker forces systemd-udevd to execute arbitrary commands as root. Affected Versions & Remediation The following Ubuntu releases ship the vulnerable set-capabilities variant of snap-confine by default: Ubuntu Desktop 26.04 Ubuntu Desktop 25.10 Ubuntu Desktop 24.04 (systems updated to current snapd packages) Organizations should apply the latest snapd updates immediately. Canonical has released patches through the Ubuntu Security Team following coordinated disclosure. Technical Details of the CVE-2026-8933 Full technical analysis, including source code references and proof-of-concept execution, is available in the Qualys Security Advisory: https://cdn2.qualys.com/advisory/2026/07/21/snap-confine-set-capabilities.txt Acknowledgments Qualys thanks the Ubuntu Security Team, in particular Eduardo Barretto and Zygmunt Krynicki at Canonical, for their rapid coordination and thorough patch review; and the linux-distros community, for their collaboration in hardening the snap ecosystem. Coordinated disclosure remains a cornerstone of responsible vulnerability research, and we value the trust and transparency built through these partnerships. Qualys QID Coverage for Detecting CVE-2026-8933 Qualys is releasing the QIDs as they become available. Please check the Qualys Vulnerability Knowledgebase for the full list of coverage. Use this QQL statement to scope your environment: operatingSystem. name: ["Ubuntu"] software:(name:"snapd") CyberSecurity Asset Management maintains a catalog of hardware and software lifecycle data built and curated by a dedicated research team, covering over 5,500 software publishers and 300,000 software releases, with automated daily updates to all CyberSecurity Asset Management customers. title: Finiture e rivestimenti per pezzi aerospaziali
summary: Finiture e rivestimenti per pezzi aerospaziali
body_text: Nella progettazione di parti per applicazioni aerospaziali entrano in gioco considerazioni che vanno oltre le sole prestazioni strutturali. È altrettanto importante scegliere la finitura giusta: una selezione accurata può contribuire ad aumentare la durata dei pezzi, migliorarne la resistenza all’usura e incrementare la protezione contro le condizioni ambientali. In alcuni casi, finiture e rivestimenti possono anche valorizzare l’aspetto estetico del pezzo. Processi di produzione per pezzi aerospaziali Il primo passo è identificare il servizio di produzione più adatto per realizzare i tuoi pezzi. Ecco una panoramica dei nostri servizi principali: Lavorazioni CNC : garantiscono precisione, superfici di alta qualità e garantiscono precisione, superfici di alta qualità e Stampa 3D : consente di realizzare geometrie molto complesse e organiche in metallo, plastica e perfino silicone, difficili da ottenere con altri processi, con in più opzioni di finitura avanzate Stampaggio a iniezione : ideale per plastiche ed elastomeri; è un processo collaudato e ad alta produttività, con numerose opzioni di finitura e il vantaggio di una produzione rapida a volumi più elevati Parte aerospaziale NASA prodotta da Protolabs Tipologie di finiture per il settore aerospaziale Raramente un pezzo è chiamato a resistere a condizioni impegnative quanto quelle tipiche del settore aerospaziale. I pezzi devono resistere a calore e freddo estremi, oltre a sollecitazioni e vibrazioni che le parti impiegate a terra non affrontano. Inoltre, devono rispettare standard rigorosi in termini di resistenza, durabilità e, in alcuni casi, anche di aspetto estetico. La finitura scelta può influire in modo significativo su queste caratteristiche. Quali opzioni sono disponibili? Finiture per metalli Elettrolucidatura: indicata quando servono superfici lisce e un’estetica di alta qualità. Può garantire una copertura uniforme anche su geometrie complesse o superfici interne Sabbiatura con abrasivo: ideale per ottenere una finitura uniforme e leggermente testurizzata, attenuando i segni di lavorazione Finiture satinate o lucidate: migliorano l’estetica e aumentano l’uniformità della superficie Finiture per plastiche Lisciatura a vapore: vapori chimici riducono le irregolarità superficiali, chiudendo in parte la porosità e migliorando, a seconda del materiale, la resistenza all’acqua Tintura e colorazione: spesso utilizzate per pezzi realizzati tramite Multi Jet Fusion (MJF) per ottenere una colorazione più uniforme dopo la stampa Altri rivestimenti Verniciatura a polvere: un pigmento in polvere aderisce elettrostaticamente al pezzo, che viene poi cotto in forno per ottenere strati uniformi. Funziona particolarmente bene sulle parti in lamiera, ma il peso aggiuntivo potrebbe non essere ideale per impieghi aerospaziali Placcatura: la placcatura elettrolitica e quella chimica possono aumentare la resistenza all’usura e contribuire a prolungare la durata dei componenti in condizioni ambientali estreme Le migliori scelte in condizioni estreme Placcatura elettrolitica Questa finitura durevole e resistente alla corrosione e all’usura applica al materiale uno strato metallico protettivo che può aiutare a preservare il materiale di base in condizioni estreme. Il processo può contribuire a prolungare la vita utile del pezzo, aiutando a gestire gli effetti delle sollecitazioni meccaniche nel tempo. È una buona scelta quando serve ridurre l’attrito tra parti in movimento. Processo di placcatura elettrolitica Le scelte migliori per la resistenza alla corrosione Prevenire la corrosione è fondamentale nelle applicazioni aerospaziali, dove longevità e sicurezza sono priorità assolute. Uno dei metodi più efficaci per proteggere dalla corrosione è la passivazione . Applicata ai metalli, questa lavorazione trasforma il ferro in un ossido di ferro più stabile sulla superficie, eliminando la principale causa del processo corrosivo. Anche se la ruggine è un ossido del ferro, è una forma instabile che tende a propagarsi e a consumare progressivamente il metallo. La passivazione, invece, favorisce la formazione di uno strato superficiale sottile e più stabile, che riduce la reattività del materiale. Per i pezzi in alluminio, in particolare, è possibile utilizzare il trattamento di conversione al cromato . Il processo agisce in modo simile alla passivazione, ma genera uno strato sottile di composti del cromo che funziona da barriera protettiva e può anche migliorare l’adesione di ulteriori rivestimenti, ad esempio vernici. L’anodizzazione è un processo che sottopone i pezzi metallici (tipicamente in alluminio) a corrente elettrica e a un bagno elettrolitico (spesso a base di acido solforico). Il metallo forma uno strato di ossido con spessore controllato che protegge il pezzo; lo strato risultante può essere poroso e quindi colorabile con tinture per ottenere un aspetto metallico più vivace. Il rivestimento è estremamente sottile, in linea con le esigenze del settore aerospaziale. Esistono due principali tipologie di anodizzazione, quindi è importante scegliere quella più adatta alla tua applicazione. Parti lavorate CNC con finitura anodizzata Impieghi e considerazioni Le diverse finiture influenzano le prestazioni e l’idoneità d’impiego dei pezzi per il settore aerospaziale. Le parti di un motore aeronautico richiedono finiture in grado di proteggere da usura e alte temperature. Le parti degli interni di un aeromobile, invece, invece, possono richiedere rivestimenti mirati a durabilità e requisiti specifici dell’ambiente di utilizzo. Ogni impiego nel settore aerospaziale presenta sfide specifiche in cui la finitura può fare la differenza. Sebbene le finiture siano un modo efficace per proteggere un pezzo o migliorarne l’estetica, è altrettanto importante progettare pensando alla durata nel tempo. L’uso di spessori di parete uniformi aiuta a ottenere finiture ottimali, soprattutto con la lisciatura a vapore. In definitiva, una finitura applicata correttamente e una progettazione attenta lavorano insieme per migliorare le prestazioni del pezzo. I servizi di produzione completi di Protolabs includono un’ampia libreria di finiture, disponibile all’interno di ciascuna linea di servizio. Il nostro team di assistenza clienti è a disposizione per supportarti nella scelta della finitura più adatta all'impiego di cui hai bisogno.

title: Why Agentic SREs Require Active Telemetry in Kubernetes
summary: Why Agentic SREs Require Active Telemetry in Kubernetes
body_text: There hasn’t been a time when software leaders haven’t talked about the essential nature of speed to market. For decades, driving operational efficiencies, eliminating manual bottlenecks and automating repetitive tasks has been the core mission of building and deploying software. We focused on doing the same work, just faster. We are now entering a critical new phase. The emergence of the Agentic SRE represents more than just the next step in automation; it is a fundamental shift toward operational autonomy. This trend is accelerating because it offers a clear path to higher efficiency, finally allowing the Site Reliability Engineering function to pivot from constant, reactive firefighting to proactive system design and innovation. This movement gives us the velocity we need to tackle the next generation of AI-enabled applications. As we bring agentic capabilities into our complex operations, especially those built on Kubernetes, a primary focus should be on establishing the core technical foundations that guarantee success and scale. The Strategic Imperative: Earning Trust Through Diagnosis The first wave of trust in your Agentic SRE is earned through accurate, fast, and affordable root cause analysis. We cannot delegate the final, high-value tasks of autonomous remediation until we have complete confidence in autonomous diagnosis. If we lack certainty in the agent’s root-cause determination, the entire system stalls as human engineers are forced to validate every decision. This simply moves the bottleneck; it doesn’t eliminate it. In our implementations today, we have found the models are already strong diagnosticians. They don’t require more training or better prompts. What they urgently need is a refined, operational context. In the operations of a Kubernetes environment, context is the fuel that drives the outcome. Without it, even a highly capable model is just a trained agent staring at a vast, inert dataset, expecting a better prompt to somehow create an understanding it doesn’t possess. Why Traditional Telemetry Falls Short for Agentic Workflows The Kubernetes observability stack has evolved to serve human operators who bring years of institutional knowledge and intuition to incident response. Traditional telemetry systems collect everything and store it passively, relying on the engineer to query, filter, and correlate signals across fragmented tools. This works when a senior SRE can synthesize patterns from experience, but it creates an insurmountable challenge for autonomous agents. Consider a typical pod failure in a production cluster. Traditional observability gives you the raw materials: logs showing an OOMKill event, metrics indicating memory pressure, traces revealing increased latency. But these signals arrive independently, timestamped but disconnected. A human engineer intuitively knows to check recent deployments, examine the service mesh configuration, and correlate this failure with similar patterns from last month. An agentic system lacks this intuition. It receives fragmented data across multiple storage systems, each requiring separate queries and different schemas. The agent must reconstruct context from scratch for every incident, burning inference cycles on correlation work that should have been done upstream. This is why most early autonomous systems plateau at symptom detection rather than root cause analysis. Active Telemetry: Engineering Context at the Data Layer Active Telemetry fundamentally reimagines the observability pipeline by performing context engineering during data ingestion rather than at query time. This approach transforms telemetry from a passive archive into an intelligent, pre-processed knowledge optimized for autonomous decision-making. The architecture operates on three core principles: Real-time processing and routing: Clean, enriched data flows that provide immediate, noise-free signals rather than delayed batch processing. This includes dynamic filtering that removes irrelevant data while preserving critical AI performance indicators. Context engineering : Providing the right signals at the right time for faster decision-making. This means correlating infrastructure events with model performance changes, understanding the full context of failures rather than just symptoms. Noise reduction: Filtering out irrelevant data while preserving critical AI performance indicators. Organizations implementing this approach report 50% data volume reduction while maintaining full operational context. This architectural shift has profound implications for autonomous operations. This isn’t because the model is better trained; it’s because the data infrastructure delivers decision-ready context rather than raw telemetry. Defining Success: Benchmarks for Organizational Impact As we move from pilot projects to an enterprise-wide strategy, defining verifiable benchmarks is key. Our metrics should measure impact and strategic value, not just activity. These metrics confirm that the Agentic SRE is not just a tool for stability, but a lever for organizational growth. Mean Time to Remediation (MTTR) : In Active Telemetry environments, we’ve observed MTTR reductions of 60-80% compared to traditional observability stacks. This improvement stems directly from eliminating the correlation overhead that dominates incident response. The strategic value extends beyond speed: freeing our most skilled SREs from repetitive triage allows them to redirect their expertise toward architectural resilience, system design, and product innovation. Prediction and Fix Accuracy : A high score here is the clearest indicator of system maturity and earned trust. Active Telemetry’s context-rich data enables pattern recognition across incidents, allowing agents to detect precursor signals that would be invisible in traditional telemetry noise. When an agent can confidently predict and prevent a cascading failure based on early warning signs, it has truly moved beyond reactive automation to proactive reliability engineering. Operational Efficiency (Cost) : The demonstrated reduction in cloud spend and RCA token consumption resulting from agents autonomously right-sizing Kubernetes resources and leveraging optimized, contextual data pipelines. Active Telemetry reduces observability costs by 40-70% through intelligent filtering and compression, while simultaneously enabling better resource optimization decisions. This establishes the SRE function as a clear, quantifiable driver of financial efficiency, not just an operational cost center. The Path Forward While scale remains a significant challenge in operating modern, cloud-native systems, the solution lies in driving that scale through improved context. Traditional telemetry architectures were designed for human consumption, creating an impedance mismatch with autonomous operations. Active Telemetry resolves this by treating context engineering as a first-class concern in the data pipeline itself. Active Telemetry transforms overwhelming data streams into decision-ready signals and becomes the foundation upon which effective AI operations are built, finally enabling agents to diagnose root causes rather than merely detect symptoms. Implementing Active Telemetry is a fundamental architectural shift that unlocks the full promise of autonomous operations in complex environments like Kubernetes. The question is no longer whether to adopt agentic workflows, but whether your telemetry infrastructure can support them at scale. ‍
